subject: general
question: In a diesel engine, heat is supplied at which of the following thermodynamic processes?
solution:
The correct answer is __At constant pressure process.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Diesel engines__ operate on the Diesel cycle, which is characterized by heat addition at constant pressure.
 
• In the Diesel cycle, air is compressed adiabatically to high pressure and temperature.
 
• Fuel is injected into the compressed air and combusts at a constant pressure.
 
• This constant pressure heat addition is the defining feature of the Diesel cycle.
 
• As a result of combustion, the temperature of the air-fuel mixture increases significantly.
 
• The high-temperature gas expands, performing work during the power stroke of the engine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Constant Pressure Process:**

 
 
• Heat is added during the constant pressure process in the Diesel cycle.
 
• This process is different from the Otto cycle, where heat is added at constant volume.
 
 
 
• **Constant Volume Process:**
 
 
• Occurs in the Otto cycle, not in the Diesel cycle.
 
• Heat addition at constant volume results in a different thermodynamic behavior.
 
 
 
• **Adiabatic Processes:**
 
 
• In both the Diesel and Otto cycles, compression and expansion are adiabatic processes.
 
• No heat is exchanged with the surroundings during these stages.
